title: Week Ahead — Market Outlook
headline: Markets enter the week with strong equity momentum but a concentrated macro and duration test as soft jobs data meets CPI, PPI, heavy Treasury supply, and AI-infrastructure earnings.
volatilityRationale: The VIX closed at 14.90 on Friday and was quoted at 15.45 Monday morning, consistent with contained rather than stressed volatility, but the calendar is dense: inflation data, a large Treasury refunding slate, and AI-linked earnings can all challenge the current risk-on narrative. A hotter inflation print, weak auction demand, or cautious AI-capex commentary could create a sharper move than the headline volatility level implies.

recap.text: The July employment report showed a surprise loss of 23,000 nonfarm jobs, while May and June payrolls were revised down by 103,000; the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% as labor-force participation declined to 61.4%.
U.S. equities finished the week higher after the soft jobs data reduced near-term expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike; Reuters said the S&P 500 closed at a record high Friday.
The Nasdaq 100 rose from 28,776.80 on August 3 to 29,722.30 on August 7, while SPY rose from 757.67 to 773.26 over the same period.

The VIX declined from 15.86 on August 3 to 14.90 on August 7 even as markets absorbed the weak labor data, signaling that investors were treating the report as a rate-relief event rather than an immediate growth shock.

triggers.text: U.S. CPI for July is scheduled for release at 8:30 a.m. ET, the week’s key inflation test for the rate path.
The Treasury refunding slate includes a 3-year note auction, followed by the 10-year note and 30-year bond; duration demand could influence yields and rate-sensitive equities.
U.S. PPI for July is scheduled for release at 8:30 a.m. ET, providing a second inflation read and a check on pipeline price pressure.

CoreWeave reports after the close, Cisco reports after the close, and Coherent reports after the close; investor focus is likely to center on AI demand, networking, data-center exposure, and capital intensity.
Applied Materials is among the week’s notable late-week earnings catalysts, adding a semiconductor-demand read-through after the CPI/PPI sequence.

watch.text: Watch the labor-market-versus-inflation tension: soft hiring supports rate relief, but a firmer CPI/PPI combination could reverse the bond and equity reaction.
Watch Treasury auction demand and the 10-year/30-year yield response; weak demand would raise the risk of duration-led pressure on high-duration growth stocks.
Watch whether AI-infrastructure earnings validate the current investment cycle through bookings and demand, or flag rising financing and capacity risks.
